chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all of them, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Tareef al-Iskaf, from al-Asbagh, from the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) that he said:

Whoever wishes to exit this world having been freed from sins like gold that has no dross, and no one demands a right from him, let him recite at the end of the five prayers the Attribution of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Say: He is Allah, One' twelve times,

then let him extend his hands and say: 'O Allah, indeed I ask You by Your Hidden, Guarded, Pure, Purified, Blessed Name, and I ask You by Your Great Name and Ancient Authority, O Giver of Gifts, O Liberator of Captives, O Freer of Necks from the Fire, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, and free my neck from the Fire, and take me out of this world safely, and make me enter Paradise unharmed, and make my supplication its beginning success, its middle passing, and its end righteousness. Indeed, You are the Knower of the Hidden.'.

Then he, peace be upon him, said: This is one of the Concealed Things which the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, taught me and ordered me to teach to Hasan and Hussain.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for purification from sins after the five daily prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the spiritual efficacy of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas twelve times after the five daily prayers as a means to achieve complete purification from sins and debts, likening the soul to pure gold. The supplication emphasizes divine names and the intercession of the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the Shia tradition of transmitting esoteric knowledge ('Khawaas') from the Prophet to Imam Ali and then to Hasan and Husayn. This practice underscores the belief in the transformative power of specific dhikr in securing freedom from the Fire and ensuring a peaceful transition to the afterlife.
